after: Two records go: Dana's private record and one open proposal that nobody reviewed yet.
Dana's approved record in `/project/example-project/shared/` is not in the list. It stays.
The line `list index` is a warning. The store answers a list from an index that lags one to five minutes behind a write. A record that a step deleted a minute ago can still be in the list.

steps.title: The apply step after Alice's word
before: Alice reads the plan and says yes. The coordinator runs the same command with `--apply`.

frame.title: coordinator on alice@desk: ~/tenant-pi
frame.source: round 4 of the live proof: the offboard apply and the check of the IAM user with the admin login

lines.text: registry: dana is offboarded and left every project list
aws: [ERROR]: An error occurred (NoSuchEntity) when calling the GetUser operation: The user with name pi-memory-person-dana cannot be found.

after: The access key is deleted before the user, so a copy of the key is useless from now on.
The registry file now gives Dana the status `offboarded`, and no project list names her.
IAM has no user `pi-memory-person-dana` any more.

A delete can fail when the list index still lists a record that is gone. The script counts such a delete (error code 404) as done. Any other failed delete stops the step before the IAM steps, and the script prints the code and the message.

steps.title: What Dana's old key gets
before: Dana still has the key in her AWS profile. She tries it.

frame.title: dana@laptop: ~
frame.source: round 4 of the live proof: a read with the deleted key of the test person

lines.text: aws bedrock-agentcore retrieve-memory-records --memory-id mem-EXAMPLE --namespace /shared/ --search-criteria searchQuery=tests --profile pi-memory-person-dana
aws: [ERROR]: An error occurred (UnrecognizedClientException) when calling the RetrieveMemoryRecords operation: The security token included in the request is invalid.

after: AWS no longer knows the key. The request fails before any policy is read. The answer is an error and no data.
The error is `UnrecognizedClientException`, not `AccessDeniedException`: AWS does not know the key at all.

AgentCore Memory: recall failed (aws_failed); turn continues

after: Each of the three queries fails. The core turns `AccessDeniedException` into the code `aws_denied` and every other AWS error into `aws_failed`. A deleted key gives `aws_failed`.
The block is empty, so the command prints no record. In Pi, the same three lines go to the standard error of the Pi process, and the turn continues without records.

learned: Offboarding is one command: a dry run first, then the apply step by the coordinator with the admin login.
The step deletes the private records, the open proposals and the rejected records of the person, then the key, the policy and the user.
Approved records stay. Their metadata still names the author.
A deleted key gets `UnrecognizedClientException` and no data. The core turns it into `aws_failed`.
The purge lists one exact rejected namespace for each person of the registry. `--person` names one namespace.
The list index lags. A step right after a delete can still list the deleted record.
cannot: Offboarding cannot delete a shared record or remove the author name from it.
The last maintainer of a project cannot be offboarded. The owner names another maintainer first.
A maintainer cannot purge. The purge needs the admin login.
The purge cannot touch `/shared/`, a project shared namespace, a proposals namespace or a private namespace.
The apply step refuses the example registry of the repository and every registry file inside it.
